findings.title: Unicode symlink pairing still fails for hard links and on Windows
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:616 — multiple identity matches fall back to single_fold; stored_name then returns None for an unpaired symlink at line 539. Reproduced on macOS: src/σ points outside the source, src/alias is a hard link to that symlink, and absolute src/ς resolves to the same inode with nlink=2. Mirror deleted dst/σ/saved.txt and its directory, exited 0, and issued no exclusion warning. The exact-spelling control preserved them. Separately, line 583 retains paired_by_case on Windows; a pure probe confirmed that it cannot pair ς with σ.
findings.predicted_failure: A valid filesystem-equivalent absolute exclude silently loses protection when the symlink has another hard-link name. Mirror deletes explicitly excluded destination data. Windows retains the same failure wherever filesystem equivalence succeeds but Unicode lowercase comparison does not.
findings.better_approach: Recover the particular directory entry's stored name through filesystem-aware, non-following lookup on each platform. Do not substitute lowercase comparison when identities have multiple names. Add hard-linked symlink survival coverage and Windows filesystem-equivalence coverage.

findings.title: Destination spelling differences still expose excluded subtrees to mirror deletion
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/fs_enum.rs:127 — subtree matching compares the destination's spelling against the source-derived case-sensitive pattern. transfer_session/mod.rs:4177 reuses that filter for destination enumeration. Reproduced on case-insensitive macOS with src/cache pointing outside, absolute exclude src/CACHE, and existing dst/Cache/saved.txt: mirror deleted the saved file and directory. The identical run with destination spelling dst/cache preserved them.
findings.predicted_failure: Even after source-name resolution succeeds, mirror deletes an excluded destination counterpart whose stored spelling differs from the source's. This leaves the earlier filesystem-case contract materially open.
findings.better_approach: Resolve literal exclusions against the destination filesystem when constructing deletion scope, preserving glob semantics and protecting equivalent destination spellings. Add a survival test where source, typed exclude, and destination use different spellings.

findings.title: Typed Unix escapes still change deletion scope on a Windows peer
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/fs_enum.rs:204 — a bare backslash becomes '/', including in received patterns. transfers/filter.rs:228 leaves Unix relative escapes unchanged before serialization. A parameterized compiler probe confirmed that wire pattern ./a\b excludes ab/saved.txt under the Unix rule but allows it under the Windows rule; Windows instead excludes a/b/saved.txt. Both destination paths are valid Windows names. This was tested through the actual rule compiler on macOS, not a Windows runtime.
findings.predicted_failure: A Unix-to-Windows mirror using --exclude './a\b' omits source ab while leaving destination ab inside deletion scope, allowing existing excluded data to be deleted. It also incorrectly protects a/b.
findings.better_approach: Translate typed Unix escapes into a portable wire representation before serialization and compile received patterns consistently. Preserve native Windows separator handling for locally supplied patterns, including .\cache.

findings.title: Windows absolute patterns still rewrite backslashes inside bracket classes
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:352 — absolute_components still replaces every backslash, bypassing the new bracket-aware normalizer. A probe of resolve_excludes_on with the Windows rule converted <root>/back[s\]lash into back[s/]lash without warning. The original glob matches backslash but not back/lash; the resulting filter excluded both backslash/saved.txt and back/lash/saved.txt. On Windows, C:\src\back[s\]lash follows this same absolute-pattern branch.
findings.predicted_failure: A valid Windows absolute exclude silently omits an unrelated subtree from copy or backup and incorrectly removes it from mirror deletion scope. build_spec also sends the corrupted pattern to peers.
findings.better_approach: Make absolute-pattern tokenization preserve bracket-class contents as well as relative-pattern normalization. Test absolute Windows patterns containing classes with both a backslash and an ordinary member.
